what_it_does: AI accelerator chips store and move sensitive model data through external memory chips, so that data needs to be encrypted and authenticated to prevent tampering. A standard authentication scheme called a Bonsai Merkle Tree (BMT) — essentially a tree of cryptographic checksums that lets hardware verify nothing has been altered — creates a significant performance bottleneck when workloads access memory in dense, rapid bursts as AI inference does. AutoSkewBMT automatically shapes the tree's geometry (which levels are wide or narrow) to match the specific access patterns of a given AI workload, finding a layout that keeps security intact while cutting the authentication overhead. The result is a tuned security structure that fits the workload rather than forcing the workload to tolerate a one-size-fits-all structure.
